investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T08:58–09:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this window was stuck Unschedulable for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is localized to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature in production-api.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both affinity-matching nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (2 out of 6) that happen to be the same nodes with exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm quota, creating a compounded constraint with no fallback.

Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new pods from being scheduled. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but a prior failed or orphaned run could have left resources allocated.

Lower confidence: A quota or limit change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the node or namespace level could have reduced available capacity, but no configuration change evidence is present in the supplied packet.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:00–09:05Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable because no preemption victims exist and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. This infrastructure-level resource exhaustion prevents the eval runner from creating any remote agent, so the remote-agent-state check never reaches the state-polling phase and produces no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T08:58–09:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this window was stuck Unschedulable for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is localized to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature in production-api.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both affinity-matching nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (2 out of 6) that happen to be the same nodes with exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm quota, creating a compounded constraint with no fallback.

Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new pods from being scheduled. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but a prior failed or orphaned run could have left resources allocated.

Lower confidence: A quota or limit change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the node or namespace level could have reduced available capacity, but no configuration change evidence is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. This resource exhaustion prevented any remote agent pod from being scheduled during the eval window, causing all three remote-agents checks to time out without producing evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes and 'No preemption victims found', meaning all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads and cannot be reclaimed (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, this could have shrunk available capacity without a corresponding increase in kata.peerpods.io/vm quota.

Tertiary — cluster-level quota or resource limit on kata.peerpods.io/vm: the total VM resource quota across the cluster may be set too low relative to concurrent eval and production workload demand, causing exhaustion under normal load.

Lower confidence — transient burst of concurrent remote agent workloads at the time of the eval run: if other jobs or users were simultaneously consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the eval window may have coincided with peak utilization rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks fail at pod scheduling time with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, preventing any agent from starting (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool on the production cluster
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly names this extended resource as exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity, and reports no preemption victims available.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes that have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

affectedAreas.label: infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs — createAgent call at line 1918
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner invokes createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; this is the earliest code boundary where the scheduling failure surfaces and prevents any evidence from being collected (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.label: infra/evals/status/features.json — remote-agents feature registry entry
affectedAreas.reason: All three failing checks are registered under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185). The feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, meaning two required-check failures (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are sufficient to trigger a feature-level outage signal (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether the resource is still exhausted or was transiently consumed at eval time.
If the resource is persistently exhausted, increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota or add additional nodes with the required affinity labels and kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to the cluster.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional. If nodes were relabeled or affinity rules were tightened, evaluate whether the schedulable pool can be safely expanded.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any capacity or affinity change to confirm recovery and that all 5 required evidence fields are returned.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184). With degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, the two required-check failures are sufficient to trigger a feature-level outage signal — prioritize restoring scheduling capacity for those two checks first.
Monitor the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool over time to detect saturation trends before they cause eval or production scheduling failures.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out the possibility that preemption could free capacity and confirms whether the nodes are fully saturated by equal- or higher-priority workloads.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a subsequent eval run with the same configuration succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the exhaustion was transient rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

If kubectl or cluster tooling shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling error may have a different root cause (e.g., a quota admission webhook or a node condition other than resource exhaustion).

If the node affinity/selector rules for remote agent pods were recently changed to exclude 4 nodes and those 4 nodes previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the root cause would be affinity misconfiguration rather than raw resource exhaustion.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, a shared scheduling dependency would be less likely and the failure would need to be localized to the runtime step specifically.

If local-agent-runtime or other non-remote checks were also failing with scheduling errors, the problem would be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool and the diagnosis would need to be widened.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on each cluster node and alerts when allocatable minus allocated falls below a configurable threshold, catching resource exhaustion before pod scheduling fails.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), catching label drift or affinity misconfiguration before it reduces the schedulable pool to a single point of failure.

Add a scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote agent pod and warns when it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), providing an early signal before the full eval timeout is reached.

Consider a synthetic canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote agent pod on a fixed schedule and reports scheduling success/failure and latency as structured evidence, independent of the full agent lifecycle checks.
